  PROBLEM: `_resume` closes outage markers even when resume operations recorded errors in `summary["errors"]`.

- scripts/provider_outage.py:619-625 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The hold-release path treats a PR as conflicted only when `mergeable_state` is `"dirty"`, so unresolved or otherwise conflicted PRs can be treated as conflict-free.
  WHY: Such PRs can have outage-only holds released and receive a review claim despite not being confirmed conflict-free; severity differed between MAJOR and NIT, with MAJOR used.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:5050-5078 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The empty-editor branch extracts only the failure marker and does not propagate provider-outage details or set the provider-unavailable environment flags.
  WHY: During a provider outage, this path posts generic retry guidance and fails to suppress downstream review-blocked labeling or alerts; severity differed between BLOCKER and MAJOR, with BLOCKER used.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1398-1427 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Reviewer logs and status files share a sorted processing list and byte budget, allowing large logs to exhaust the budget before status files are read.
  WHY: Missing status evidence can cause provider-outage detection to misclassify a partial failure or miss an outage.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:525-571 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `record` calls can each create and accept their own outage marker when stale re-list results show only the caller's issue.
  WHY: The calls can both report `action=created` and emit alerts, leaving duplicate open markers; confidence differed between 3 and 4, with 4 used.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:594-700 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Resume filters PRs by `updated_at` against a `window_start` derived from the outage marker's later `created_at`.
  WHY: The PR whose failure triggered the marker can fall before the window and be skipped permanently; severity differed between BLOCKER and MAJOR, with BLOCKER used.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:251-277 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `latest_review_outcome` recognizes editor-summary comments without checking that they belong to the current head SHA.
  WHY: A summary for a different head can override the current provider-outage failure and prevent that PR from being resumed; severity differed between MAJOR and NIT, with MAJOR used.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:103-167 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `provider-outage-probe` job has no job-level concurrency group preventing overlapping probe and resume executions.
  WHY: Overlapping executions can duplicate resume comments, dispatches, label operations, and recovery alerts; severity differed between MAJOR and NIT, with MAJOR used.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:691-700 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_resume` does not persist handled work to the marker before each irreversible resume step.
  WHY: A late failure can leave no durable record of partially completed work beyond the in-memory summary.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:410 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The provider probe has no max-age bail-out for a persistently failing probe model.
  WHY: A misconfigured or retired probe model can keep the outage marker open and review dispatches skipped indefinitely.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:410 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Probe enablement is independent of `WORKFLOW_HEAL_ENABLED`.
  WHY: The probe can continue running when workflow healing is disabled, including making scheduled probe requests despite there being no marker to recover.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/provider_outage.py: 727-728 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_resume` unconditionally closes every outage marker after posting the resume comment, even when `summary["errors"]` is non-empty.
  WHY: A consumer repo whose PR listing, dispatch, or label removal failed during restore will be permanently stranded because the next tick finds no open marker and never retries the failed PRs or consumer repos.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: 624 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `resume_repo` passes `pull.get("mergeable_state") == "dirty"` as the `conflicted` argument to `hold_is_outage_only`.
  WHY: A PR with `mergeable: false` and `mergeable_state: "behind"` or `"blocked"` is treated as conflict-free, allowing an outage-only hold release claim on a conflicted PR.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: 5050-5066 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The empty-editor marker branch passes provider-log arguments to `autofix-failure-fingerprint` but extracts only `marker=`, does not export provider-unavailable flags, and posts the generic retry comment.
  WHY: When the reviewer panel fails with a provider error, the PR gets a generic retry message and downstream steps can still label it `ai:review-blocked` and send a Telegram failure alert.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: 525-563 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `record` invocations can each see an empty marker list, create an issue, and accept their own issue as the marker when GitHub's re-list is stale.
  WHY: Both calls can emit `action=created` with `alert=True`, producing multiple open outage markers and operator alerts.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: 1398-1427 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Reviewer log files and status files share a sorted processing sequence and byte budget, allowing large reviewer logs to exhaust the budget before status files are read.
  WHY: Missing status evidence can incorrectly classify a provider outage or suppress one that should have been detected.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: 694-696, specifically `window_start = parse_time(primary.get("created_at")) or now` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_resume` uses the marker issue's `created_at` as the outage window start.
  WHY: The PR that first triggered the marker can have an earlier `updated_at` and be skipped by the resume filter, leaving it paused.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: 272-273 (`latest_review_outcome`, editor summary match) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `latest_review_outcome` matches editor-summary comments by text pattern without verifying that the summary belongs to the current head SHA.
  WHY: A summary for a different head can override the latest failure outcome and prevent the outage-paused PR from being re-dispatched.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml: 109 (the `provider-outage-probe` job definition, no `concurrency:` key) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `provider-outage-probe` job has no `concurrency:` group, so overlapping ticks can run the probe simultaneously.
  WHY: Concurrent resumes can duplicate comments, review dispatches, label removal, and alerts.
TASK_GAP
Requirement: Every new tracked script in `scripts/` must be listed in `docs/INVENTORY.md` under the Scripts section, per the repository's inventory parity gate (`tests/inventory_parity.py:253-269`) which CI runs at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1087-1090`. The implement-plan lesson from PR #5864 explicitly states: "a new `scripts/` file needs its `docs/INVENTORY.md` entry in the same PR."
Expected change site: `docs/INVENTORY.md`, Scripts section, in alphabetical order near `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_autofix_report.sh` (line 269)
Evidence of absence: `grep provider_outage docs/INVENTORY.md` returns zero matches. The new `scripts/provider_outage.py` has no entry in the Scripts section. The `pr_changed_files.txt` does not list `docs/INVENTORY.md`.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
TASK_GAP
Requirement: The plan at `docs/plans/issue-5773-provider-outage-wait-and-resume-plan.md:87` specifies "CLI `record`, `status`, `tick`". The `build_parser()` in `scripts/provider_outage.py:788-818` registers only `record` and `tick` subcommands.
Expected change site: `scripts/provider_outage.py:788-818` (`build_parser()`), a `sub.add_parser("status")` call
Evidence of absence: The parser has `sub.add_parser("record")` at line 802 and `sub.add_parser("tick")` at line 821. There is no `sub.add_parser("status")` call. The plan's intent may have been satisfied by the `PROVIDER_OUTAGE_TICK` log output (which is effectively a status report), but the plan's enumerated list is unambiguous: `record`, `status`, `tick`. If `status` was intentionally dropped, the plan should note it in the PR description.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
